sentences.en: And also, a sense that, you know, the way that crises get solved is that somebody comes in and helps you a whole bunch.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们还会觉得解决危机的方式就是有人介入并给予大量帮助。

sentences.en: You know, they call the parent of the other kid, they, you know, hire a tutor.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们给另一个孩子的父母打电话，或者雇个家教。

sentences.en: And what I'm interested in instead, you know, from parents who can be more restrained, right?
sentences.zh: 而我感兴趣的是，那些能够保持克制的父母，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is not to say just letting kids hang out high and dry, but for parents who can say, you know, I can see you're very, very upset, you know, do you want some tea?
sentences.zh: 这并不是说让孩子们孤立无援，而是那些能说“我看得出你非常非常难过，你想喝点茶吗？”的父母。

sentences.en: You know, would it help if we just hung out together here for a little while?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们在这里待一会儿会有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Or do you want some time alone?
sentences.zh: 或者你想一个人待会儿？

sentences.en: When parents hold back a little and don't step in a helicopter, what young people get to discover is that emotions are very rarely like fires.
sentences.zh: 当父母稍微退后一点，不去做“直升机父母”时，年轻人会发现情绪很少像火灾一样。

sentences.en: They're much more like waves, you know, that they, they rise and they crest and then they flow away.
sentences.zh: 它们更像是波浪，你知道，它们升起、达到顶峰，然后消退。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the things I remember learning in my training is, you know, with a hard feeling, the only way out is through, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，我记得在培训中学到的一件事是，面对痛苦的情绪，唯一的出路就是经历它，对吧？

sentences.en: You just have it.
sentences.zh: 你只需要去感受它。

sentences.en: And when we create time and space for young people to discover this about how emotions work, you know, two things happen that are really important.
sentences.zh: 当我们为年轻人创造时间和空间去发现情绪是如何运作的时，两件非常重要的事情就会发生。

sentences.en: First of all, emotions become much less frightening because you're like, oh yeah, no, I'm having a big one.
sentences.zh: 首先，情绪变得不那么可怕了，因为你会想，哦，是的，我正在经历一场大的情绪波动。

sentences.en: You know, let me ride it out and then I'll feel better after a good cry, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，让我顺其自然，大哭一场后我会感觉好些，对吧？

sentences.en: Like that's such a great thing for young people to learn.
sentences.zh: 这对年轻人来说是非常棒的学习过程。

sentences.en: The other thing they learn is it's basically an autonomous system, right?
sentences.zh: 他们学到的另一件事是，这基本上是一个自主系统，对吧？

sentences.en: That they don't need anybody else for it.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要任何人的帮助。

sentences.en: And it's, I mean, it's really nice if a living person wants to sort of be there with you and be patient and quiet while you're having your moment.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果有人愿意陪着你，在你经历情绪波动时保持耐心和安静，那确实很好。

sentences.en: But what a gift, right?
sentences.zh: 但这真是一份礼物，对吧？

sentences.en: To, to model this total comfort with the stress, which then helps young people feel more at ease with the stress when it does occur.
sentences.zh: 去示范这种对压力的完全从容，这反过来能帮助年轻人在压力真正出现时感到更自在。

sentences.en: So at the most sort of granular level,
sentences.zh: 所以，在最细致的层面上，

sentences.en: we can rob young people of a chance to discover that humans are built in a way that we actually are pretty self-correcting or self-writing.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会剥夺年轻人发现人类天生具有自我纠正或自我修复能力的机会。

sentences.en: And then we can, of course, take that up many, many levels, you know, to, if there's a problem with the teacher, you know, the parent intervening,
sentences.zh: 当然，我们可以把这个层面提升到更高，比如如果老师有问题，父母介入，

sentences.en: if there's a problem with an application, the parent intervening, you know, never sort of learning
sentences.zh: 如果申请有问题，父母介入，永远学不会

sentences.en: how to self-correct or that in some cases there's sort of an automatic self-correction that will occur.
sentences.zh: 如何自我纠正，或者学不会在某些情况下会自动发生自我纠正。

sentences.en: So how can parents and families help teens embrace stress and realize the difference between unhealthy stress and healthy stress?
sentences.zh: 那么父母和家庭如何帮助青少年拥抱压力，并意识到不健康压力和健康压力之间的区别呢？

sentences.en: Well, so the first thing we've got to do is even articulate that there is healthy stress, um, and teach young people that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们首先要做的就是明确指出存在“健康压力”，并教导年轻人这一点。

sentences.en: And I think one of the easiest way to do that is to, one of the easiest ways is to, um, talk about stress in the same way we talk about weight lifting, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为最简单的方法之一就是，嗯，用我们谈论举重的方式来谈论压力，对吧？

sentences.en: That if you want to build muscle, you have to lift weights that are heavy enough to be uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 如果你想锻炼肌肉，你必须举起足够重、让你感到不舒服的重量。

sentences.en: And what happens is that when you lift weights, eventually your muscles adapt,
sentences.zh: 当你举重时，你的肌肉最终会适应，

sentences.en: you know, they gain strength and what was difficult becomes easier at which point, you know, we move you up to heavier weights.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们会增强力量，原本困难的事情会变得容易，这时我们就会让你增加重量。

sentences.en: So school stress, which is a lot of stress, you know, that kids manage is just like that.
sentences.zh: 所以学校的压力，也就是孩子们管理的大量压力，就像这样。

sentences.en: You know, when you get new material, when you get to a new grade, when you take a new hard class, at first it's very, very stressful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你接触新教材、进入新学年、选修新的高难度课程时，起初压力会非常非常大。

sentences.en: It's new, it's heavier, it's harder than you're used to.
sentences.zh: 它是新的，更重，比你习惯的更难。

sentences.en: If you stick with it, you will soon adapt, your capacities will expand and you gain strength, intellectual strength that you get to keep.
sentences.zh: 如果你坚持下去，你很快就会适应，你的能力会扩展，你会获得力量，一种你可以保留的智力力量。

sentences.en: And as soon as you've got it, we're going to give you harder work.
sentences.zh: 一旦你掌握了，我们就会给你更难的任务。

sentences.en: So we can help teenagers embrace stress by acknowledging that there is such a thing as healthy stress.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以通过承认“健康压力”的存在来帮助青少年拥抱压力。

sentences.en: And though it is not pleasant, we can say, but here's the benefit.
sentences.zh: 虽然它并不令人愉快，但我们可以说，好处在这里。

sentences.en: This is how you get a lot smarter.
sentences.zh: 这就是你变得更聪明的方法。

sentences.en: This is how you really build your intellectual capacities.
sentences.zh: 这就是你真正建立智力能力的方法。

sentences.en: And then in terms of unhealthy stress, that's where we need to focus on recovery.
sentences.zh: 至于不健康的压力，那才是我们需要关注恢复的地方。

sentences.en: Because like I said, the stress of school is doable if there's an opportunity for recovery.
sentences.zh: 因为就像我说的，如果有恢复的机会，学校的压力是可以应对的。

sentences.en: And so helping teenagers really know how they recover, how they like to recover, doing that, moving right to it, doing it efficiently, creating space for it can make
sentences.zh: 所以帮助青少年真正了解他们如何恢复、他们喜欢如何恢复，并付诸行动，高效地去做，为之创造空间，可以产生

sentences.en: a big difference.
sentences.zh: 巨大的差异。

sentences.en: A few times during our conversation, we've talked about the need for parents to deal with their own
sentences.zh: 在我们的谈话中，我们几次提到了父母需要处理他们自己的

sentences.en: anxiety.
sentences.zh: 焦虑。

sentences.en: But I imagine, you know, for parents who are who have read your book or listening right now, they might feel alarmed by these statistics and quite worried.
sentences.zh: 但我可以想象，对于那些读过你的书或正在收听的父母来说，他们可能会对这些统计数据感到惊慌和担忧。

sentences.en: So what advice do you have to keep for parents to keep calm so then they can then help their teen?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于父母如何保持冷静，从而帮助他们的青少年，你有什么建议？

sentences.en: I think parents should feel very reassured by how much power they have here.
sentences.zh: 我认为父母应该对他们在这里拥有的力量感到非常安心。

sentences.en: That if parents can be calm, we know from research, it makes a tremendous difference in terms of the likelihood of their child becoming unusually anxious.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，如果父母能保持冷静，这对孩子变得异常焦虑的可能性有巨大的影响。

sentences.en: So the statistics are worrisome, but the news is good.
sentences.zh: 所以统计数据令人担忧，但好消息是，

sentences.en: There's a huge amount we can do.
sentences.zh: 我们能做的事情非常多。

sentences.en: And, you know, then we can do it at a lot of levels over time.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们可以随着时间的推移在很多层面上做到这一点。

sentences.en: You know, we can help young people manage their friendships with one another.
sentences.zh: 我们可以帮助年轻人处理彼此之间的友谊。

sentences.en: We can help them manage the romantic landscape, which is really, really anxiety-provoking for them, you know, by
sentences.zh: 我们可以帮助他们处理浪漫关系，这对他们来说真的非常令人焦虑，你知道，通过

sentences.en: talking about, you know, gendered relationships in the healthiest possible ways.
sentences.zh: 以尽可能健康的方式谈论性别关系。

sentences.en: We can give them strategies for managing at school and also for girls in particular.
sentences.zh: 我们可以给他们提供应对学校压力的策略，特别是对于女孩。

sentences.en: Think with them about what the culture asks and equip them to be shielded a bit from some of the really unfair expectations that our culture does hold for girls and young women.
sentences.zh: 和她们一起思考文化的要求，并装备她们，使她们免受我们文化对女孩和年轻女性的一些非常不公平的期望的影响。

sentences.en: So there's much, much we can do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们能做的还有很多很多。

sentences.en: And I really think parents should feel, you know, kind of delighted that this one is much more in their hands than they may have otherwise felt was true.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为父母应该感到高兴，因为这件事比他们原本以为的更掌握在他们自己手中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And overall, what do you think are the most pressing challenges facing young people today?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，你认为当今年轻人面临的最紧迫的挑战是什么？

sentences.en: Boys and girls?
sentences.zh: 男孩和女孩？

sentences.en: We ask a lot of young people today.
sentences.zh: 我们对当今的年轻人要求很高。

sentences.en: They are, I mean, accomplishing things academically in high school that, you know, are very unlike what their own parents were accomplishing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在高中取得的学术成就，与他们父母当年取得的成就非常不同。

sentences.en: They are flooded with information.
sentences.zh: 他们被信息淹没了。

sentences.en: They have constant access to one another, which is sometimes fun, but I think is often very tiring.
sentences.zh: 他们可以随时联系彼此，这有时很有趣，但我认为这通常非常累人。

sentences.en: I think those are all very big challenges.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是非常大的挑战。

sentences.en: I think another thing I worry about
sentences.zh: 我认为我担心的另一件事是

sentences.en: is we don't talk very well about young people.
sentences.zh: 我们对年轻人的评价并不客观。

sentences.en: That when you look at how young people are described in the media, you know, it tends to sort of fall into these kind of negative stereotypes of,
sentences.zh: 当你观察媒体对年轻人的描述时，你知道，它往往倾向于陷入这些负面刻板印象，

sentences.en: you know, they're kind of naughty or they're, you know, they're doing the wrong thing or they're not, you know, doing what the adults want them to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们很淘气，或者他们在做错事，或者他们没有做成年人希望他们做的事。

sentences.en: And, you know, we have the data that we are, we are raising the best behaved generation of teenagers on record.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们有数据表明，我们正在培养有记录以来表现最好的一代青少年。

sentences.en: You know, they, they do fewer drugs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们吸毒更少。

sentences.en: They're delaying sex.
sentences.zh: 他们推迟了性行为。

sentences.en: They, if they are having sex, they're using contraception.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有性行为，他们会使用避孕措施。

sentences.en: They drink less.
sentences.zh: 他们喝酒更少。

sentences.en: Um, you know, and there's some little blips here and there in the data, but, you know, in the broad strokes, these are really good kids.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，数据中偶尔会有一些小波动，但总的来说，这些孩子真的很棒。

sentences.en: And so I actually think we should add to the stresses that teenagers face is that people don't really give them credit for how much they're
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上认为我们应该补充一点，青少年面临的压力之一是人们并没有真正认可他们所取得的成就，

sentences.en: accomplishing, how, um, thoughtful they are.
sentences.zh: 以及他们是多么体贴。

sentences.en: And that we're often instead focusing on, um, behaviors that relative to previous generations, uh, this is a really, really good group of kids.
sentences.zh: 我们往往反而专注于一些行为，而与前几代人相比，这是一群非常非常好的孩子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的很迷人。

sentences.en: If we do give teens enough credit, you know, to obviously they need people to guide them in their lives to make good decisions.
sentences.zh: 如果我们确实给予青少年足够的信任，显然他们需要有人在生活中引导他们做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: But, you know, as we've, the theme that's come up in our conversation is the fact that a lot of times
sentences.zh: 但是，正如我们谈话中出现的主题，很多时候

sentences.en: teens can figure things out on their own, or they should at least be given the chance to do that.
sentences.zh: 青少年可以自己解决问题，或者至少应该给他们机会去这样做。

sentences.en: And that, you know, according to those, you know, recent stats from the CDC, teens are using drugs less, drinking alcohol less, having sex less often with fewer partners.
sentences.zh: 而且，根据CDC的最新统计数据，青少年吸毒更少，饮酒更少，性行为更少，伴侣也更少。

sentences.en: So you said, we are raising a good generation of, of young people, but at the same time, we're also looking to all, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以你说，我们正在培养一代优秀的年轻人，但与此同时，我们也在关注所有那些

sentences.en: looking at all the things that aren't going well, or the people who feel, um, anxiety or depression or feelings of hopelessness.
sentences.zh: 进展不顺利的事情，或者那些感到焦虑、抑郁或绝望感的人。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, do you have any more thoughts on that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，你对此还有什么想法吗？

sentences.en: I think kids live up to expectations and kids live down to them.
sentences.zh: 我认为孩子会达到期望，也会辜负期望。

sentences.en: And so we never want to gloss over real problems and there are, you know, worrisome increases in, in the suicide numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以我们永远不想掩盖真正的问题，自杀人数确实有令人担忧的增长。

sentences.en: Um, and we need to take those very, very seriously, but I do worry how it feels to be a young person who is so plugged into the media
sentences.zh: 我们需要非常非常认真地对待这些问题，但我确实担心，作为一个如此沉迷于媒体的年轻人，当消息往往是你已经崩溃或你做得不对时，会有什么感觉。

sentences.en: when so often the message is that you're broken or you're not doing it right.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑其中是否存在自我实现的预言的危险，你知道，一种感觉，即

sentences.en: And I wonder if there can be within that a danger of a self-fulfilling prophecy, you know, a sense that, you know,
sentences.zh: 情绪很容易失控，而事实上，大多数年轻人对情绪的管理其实非常好。

sentences.en: emotions can so readily be out of control when in fact, most young people manage their emotions really very well.
sentences.zh: 大多数年轻人其实非常善于管理自己的情绪。

sentences.en: So I think we have to both be vigilant and take very seriously, um, trends that, you know, are moving in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们既要保持警惕，也要非常认真地对待那些朝着错误方向发展的趋势。

sentences.en: And at the same time, I think, you know, we know so much in psychology about how to take care of, um, people who are suffering that I would love to think that we get
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我认为心理学界在如何照顾那些正在受苦的人方面已经积累了丰富的知识，我很乐意看到我们能

sentences.en: our voice in there to say, yeah, you know, there, there are things we can do though.
sentences.zh: 发出自己的声音，告诉大家：是的，我们确实可以做些什么。

sentences.en: And there's ways to prevent feeling unduly anxious.
sentences.zh: 而且有办法可以防止产生过度的焦虑感。

sentences.en: Um, and if you do suffer with depression, we can really treat that, you know, and to continue to advocate for, um, all of the ways in which human beings are resilient
sentences.zh: 如果你确实患有抑郁症，我们完全可以进行治疗。我们要继续倡导人类所具备的各种韧性，

sentences.en: and can be helped to be resilient, that it doesn't have to be such a dark story.
sentences.zh: 以及如何帮助人们培养这种韧性，生活并不一定非要那么灰暗。

sentences.en: I want to touch on your column a little bit for the New York times.
sentences.zh: 我想聊聊你为《纽约时报》撰写的专栏。

sentences.en: I mean, what are the topics that seem to get the best reception from, from readers?
sentences.zh: 哪些话题最受读者欢迎？

sentences.en: You know, it's such a funny thing.
sentences.zh: 这真是一件有趣的事。

sentences.en: Um, sometimes it's a really timely topic.
sentences.zh: 有时是一些非常及时的话题。

sentences.en: Um, I wrote a piece called parenting the fortnight addict.
sentences.zh: 我写过一篇名为《如何教导“堡垒之夜”成瘾的孩子》的文章。

sentences.en: Um, and that piece just got a ton of traction because fortnight just came up, swallowed a whole bunch of kids before parents even knew what had happened.
sentences.zh: 那篇文章引起了巨大的反响，因为《堡垒之夜》刚出现时，在家长还没反应过来之前，就已经吸引了大量孩子。

sentences.en: And you know, what was so fun about that, that, that particular column, and this is my favorite
sentences.zh: 那篇专栏最有趣的地方在于——这也是我写专栏最喜欢的部分——

sentences.en: part about getting to write this column is that I got to actually unpack all of our psychological
sentences.zh: 我能够真正地拆解我们所有的心理学研究，

sentences.en: research about how video games work in terms of, you know, basically an intermittent reinforcement
sentences.zh: 解释电子游戏在“间歇性强化”机制上的运作原理，

sentences.en: schedule and various other things, um, you know, and describe that to a, to a general audience.
sentences.zh: 以及其他各种因素，并将其通俗易懂地传达给大众。

sentences.en: But then sometimes it's the columns about really timeless issues.
sentences.zh: 但有时，那些探讨永恒议题的专栏也会很受欢迎。

sentences.en: So other columns that I've written that have gotten a lot of traction, I mean, basically people are just desperate for any help with their teenagers.
sentences.zh: 我写过其他一些引起广泛关注的专栏，基本上是因为人们迫切需要应对青少年的方法。

sentences.en: People want to connect to their teenagers.
sentences.zh: 人们渴望与自己的孩子建立联系。

sentences.en: They like their teenagers.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢自己的孩子。

sentences.en: And even when their teenagers great, that doesn't always mean their teenagers being great at home with them.
sentences.zh: 即使孩子在外面表现很好，也不代表他们在家里也能和父母相处融洽。

sentences.en: So, you know, in some ways it's easy to get traction with columns on teenagers.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某些方面，关于青少年的专栏很容易引起共鸣。

sentences.en: Um, but others, you know, take up questions.
sentences.zh: 但其他一些专栏则探讨了不同的问题。

sentences.en: Like I wrote one about why teenagers become allergic to their parents, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如我写过一篇关于为什么青少年会对父母产生“过敏反应”的文章，

sentences.en: and just that moment, you know, and often sort of 13 is the height of it where like nothing the parent does is okay.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉，通常在13岁时达到顶峰，仿佛父母做什么都不对。

sentences.en: And you know, that one, you know, just got a tremendous response.
sentences.zh: 那篇文章也获得了巨大的反响。

sentences.en: And I wrote, I recently wrote one about, um, how to give advice to a teenager.
sentences.zh: 我最近还写了一篇关于如何给青少年提建议的文章。

sentences.en: Um, it was, it was around, it was around the holiday time.
sentences.zh: 那是在假期前后写的。

sentences.en: And I think the headline was, you know, how to wrap a gift, how to wrap advice as a gift your teenager might open.
sentences.zh: 标题大概是：如何包装建议，让它成为孩子愿意接受的礼物。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because I think this is sort of one of those kind of perennial problems that parents have, you know, they've got all these really, you know, terrific
sentences.zh: 因为我认为这是家长们面临的永恒难题之一，他们有很多非常棒的建议

sentences.en: things they want to share with their teenager and they cannot seem to do it in any way that gets a satisfying response or even a response.
sentences.zh: 想要分享给孩子，却似乎总找不到一种方式能得到满意的回应，甚至得不到任何回应。

sentences.en: So, um, you know, I, I really try to sort of move around in, in what I write about both from the, you know, immediate concern things.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实尝试在写作中兼顾各种主题，既有那些迫在眉睫的担忧，

sentences.en: So obviously I've written a fair bit about stress and anxiety, um, to the sort of universals of family life that are difficult, uh, but normal.
sentences.zh: 比如我写过不少关于压力和焦虑的文章，也探讨了家庭生活中那些虽困难但正常的普遍问题。

sentences.en: Um, and just to try to really use, you know, the training I got, um, and to make it available to a broad audience.
sentences.zh: 我只是想利用我所受的专业训练，让更多大众受益。

sentences.en: You know, I think that that's a real thing that, um, you know, I'm always so grateful to see psychologists writing, um, for, for, you know, general audiences because,
sentences.zh: 我认为心理学家为大众写作是一件非常有意义的事，我对此一直心怀感激，因为

sentences.en: you know, we know a lot and, and it's not always well described by the media and we can do a good job of it.
sentences.zh: 我们掌握了很多知识，但媒体往往描述得不够准确，而我们完全可以做得更好。

sentences.en: Um, you know, I want to talk a little bit more about Fortnite briefly.
sentences.zh: 我想简单再聊聊《堡垒之夜》。

sentences.en: Um, you know, it's taken the world by storm and, you know, parents seem to be struggling to keep their kids away from the game.
sentences.zh: 它风靡全球，家长们似乎很难让孩子远离这款游戏。

sentences.en: Um, because it is a very social game.
sentences.zh: 因为它是一款社交性很强的游戏。

sentences.en: You can, you can be on it on your phone, on a good game console, on a computer, it's really everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你可以在手机、游戏主机、电脑上玩，它真的无处不在。

sentences.en: Um, but how can parents manage their kids gaming overall?
sentences.zh: 那么，家长该如何管理孩子的游戏行为呢？

sentences.en: You know, I would probably say in the same way, you know, I would start with the same advice I gave around managing technology in general, you know, first
sentences.zh: 我可能会说，这和我之前给出的关于管理科技产品的建议是一样的。首先，

sentences.en: draw lines around what you're trying to protect.
sentences.zh: 要为你想要保护的东西划定界限。

sentences.en: Um, and we have these things and, you know, and doing those things, you know, sleeping, studying, being with the family, getting physical
sentences.zh: 我们有这些基本需求，比如睡眠、学习、家庭时光、体育锻炼，

sentences.en: activity, you know, those will keep a kid pretty busy.
sentences.zh: 如果能保证这些，孩子的生活就会很充实。

sentences.en: Um, if we, if we protect them at the levels they deserve to be protected at.
sentences.zh: 只要我们能在应有的程度上保护好这些底线。

sentences.en: Um, and, and so start there, you know, so you might even, you know, just to paraphrase again, like you might say, it's not that I'm against gaming,
sentences.zh: 所以从这里开始。换句话说，你可能会告诉孩子：并不是我反对玩游戏，

sentences.en: it's that I'm for sleep, you know, so the sleep's a non-negotiable.
sentences.zh: 而是我支持睡眠，睡眠是不可妥协的。

sentences.en: Um, and then I think, you know, from there it becomes very specific to families, you know, where they set limits on it,
sentences.zh: 然后，我认为这取决于每个家庭的具体情况，看他们如何设定限制。

sentences.en: you know, and I've seen families do a whole bunch of different things from, you know, it's only on
sentences.zh: 我见过各种各样的做法，比如只在周末玩，

sentences.en: the weekends or it's a limited amount of time per day, or, you know, um, you have to self-regulate
sentences.zh: 或者每天限制时间，或者要求孩子学会自我调节，

sentences.en: and if you can't, I will, you know, I think there's a lot of different ways for parents to manage it.
sentences.zh: 如果做不到，家长再介入。我认为有很多方法可以管理。

sentences.en: Um, but we do want to see that kids have variety in their lives.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实希望看到孩子们的生活丰富多彩。

sentences.en: You know, it's just not healthy to just do one thing all the time.
sentences.zh: 一直只做一件事是不健康的。

sentences.en: And, you know, certainly, um, there are kids who really get lost in gaming and, um, and, and, you know, that's a moment where the parent needs to find a way to
sentences.zh: 当然，确实有些孩子沉迷于游戏，那种时候家长就需要想办法

sentences.en: insist on some variety in terms of how their time is spent.
sentences.zh: 坚持让孩子的生活方式多样化。

sentences.en: So all is not loSt.
sentences.zh: 所以一切并没有无可救药。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: Some of the articles I was reading, it seems like the parents have just kind of
sentences.zh: 我读到的一些文章显示，家长们似乎已经放弃了，

sentences.en: thrown up their hands or just at their wits end.
sentences.zh: 或者已经束手无策了。

sentences.en: I don't know what it was, but I think it's, it's like, it's important that you said just to, all is not loSt. There are still boundaries that
sentences.zh: 我不知道具体情况，但你刚才说得对，一切并没有无可救药。依然可以设定界限，

sentences.en: can be set and, you know, maybe phrasing it in a, is it not a deprivation, but what you're gaining from limiting screen time.
sentences.zh: 也许换个说法，这不是剥夺，而是限制屏幕时间能带来的益处。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There are things that have to happen and gaming is not one of them.
sentences.zh: 有些事情是必须完成的，而玩游戏并不在其中。
